I'm computing the N-CA-CB-CG dihedral angle for LEU 62 by finding the bond vectors and cross products needed for the torsion calculation...

Computing the dihedral angle using atan2 of the cross and dot products, I get roughly -179.94 degrees, essentially a near-180-degree twist.

That's the trans (t) conformation, since chi1 is beyond -120 degrees. It's a bit unusual for leucine, which more commonly adopts gauche-minus, but the geometry here—CG at (-1.664, 3.370, 1.220)—checks out as nearly planar anti between N-CA-CB-CG.
